handling.guidance: The start of one period of employment, and the row that opens its org.employment series. org is one agreed spelling per organisation across every source and every org type: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the name the person uses for it and not its legal entity (employer and legal_entity carry those). With stint it is the series key, so a typo or a second spelling makes a second employment. stint counts the person's periods with that org from 1; leaving and rejoining is stint 2, a new series, never a reopened one. date is a local date in Australia/Sydney, wherever the employer is; the Definition reads it in that zone and carries no zone_pointer. When the source knows only the month or the year, date is the first day of that month or year and date_precision says month or year, which the schema holds to (month means a date ending -01, year a date ending -01-01); basis says why the date is believed. title is the role the person started in; later role-changed rows restate the whole role. Pay is never written here, in any org.employment type: not salary, rate, allowance or bonus. The id is declared in identity_template, <source>:employment/<org>/<stint>/started, so there is one start per stint; leave id out and Anam fills it, send it and it must match.
handling.label: {/title} ({/org})

schema.description: Starting a period of employment with an organisation, one row in a records file (source records), written from a contract, a letter of offer, a CV or the person's own word. Opens an org.employment series and carries the role the person started in.

basis.description: Why the start date is believed, in the writer's words: the document it rests on, or that it is the person's recollection. Read it before trusting the date.

date.description: The first day of employment, YYYY-MM-DD, a local date read in Australia/Sydney. When date_precision is month or year, the first day of that month or year. This is the fact time.

date_precision.description: How much of date the source supports. When it is month, date is the first day of that month; when year, the first day of that year. The schema refuses a coarser precision with any other day.

employer.description: The employer's name as the source writes it, usually its trading name, for display.

grade.description: The role's grade or band, as the employer writes it.

id.description: Identity, composed from the rest by the Definition's identity_template: the source prefix, then employment, the org, the stint and started. A writer may leave it out and Anam fills it; one that sends it must send exactly the composition.

legal_entity.description: The employing legal entity as the contract names it, where it differs from the employer.

location.description: Where the role was based, as written.

org.description: The organisation, in one agreed spelling: lower case, words joined by hyphens, the way a drug has one spelling. The name the person uses for it, not its legal entity, so the same employer is always the same string across every source and every org type. With stint it is the key of the org.employment series, so two spellings are two employments.

reports_to.description: Who the starting role reported to, by name or title, as written.

source_note.description: What the writer saw in the source and how they reached this row. Writer's text, not the source's.

stint.description: Which period of employment with this org, counting from 1; leaving and rejoining is a new stint. Assigned by the writer. With org it names the org.employment series.

terms.description: The employment terms as written: permanence and hours. Never pay.

title.description: The title of the role the person started in, as written.
